title: Evidence Signal Ingestor and Proof Normalizer for Regional Retention
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Build an event-driven evidence ingestion and normalization pipeline that converts heterogeneous control artifacts (logs, snapshots, manifests, telemetry traces) into a canonical 'evidence envelope' for regional retention and automated audit export. This work focuses on the signal ingestor (frontline event handler), normalizer (schema mapping + enrichment), signer/timestamp step (KMS-backed attestation), and per-region immutable manifest generation. The goal is to reduce manual evidence assembly time for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits and ensure tamper-evident artifacts are produced and stored in region-locked buckets with retention metadata.

Scope:
- Implement a lightweight Evidence Signal Ingestor service that consumes brokered messages (Kafka topic: evidence.signals) and small-file uploads (S3 presigned callback) and emits normalized artifacts to the Evidence Normalizer queue.
- Define and implement 'evidence envelope v2' JSON schema (fields: envelope_id, source_timestamp, region, control_id, artifact_type, canonical_payload_ref, retention_policy_id, signature_block).
- Normalizer will canonicalize payloads (strip sensitive transient fields, add retention tags, map control IDs to control matrix), extract minimal indexable metadata (control, region, customer, time range) and store canonical objects in s3 path per-region with versioned manifests.
- Add a signer/timestamp stage that attaches a KMS ECDSA signature and RFC3161-style timestamp token to the envelope; record signature metadata in the manifest.
- Generate a per-bundle manifest manifest.json (SHA256 checksums, envelope IDs, signed_by, timestamp) and publish a read-only manifest pointer to the audit index (evidence-index-v2).
- Backfill adapter: provide a small utility to re-ingest existing archived artifacts into the v2 pipeline for customers with active retention rules.

Non-goals: full UI in Console, cross-region replication policies (handled by Dedicated infra team), long-term analytics UI (handled by Console/Observability project).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Evidence Signal Ingestor consumes sample messages and S3 callbacks; 2) Normalizer emits envelopes conforming to evidence-envelope-v2 JSON schema and stores in s3://redwood-evidence/{region}/{customer}/{envelope_id}.json; 3) Every envelope has a signature_block produced by KMS and an RFC3161 timestamp token; 4) A per-bundle manifest.json is generated and registered in evidence-index-v2; 5) Demo run with two customers (us-west-2, eu-west-1) showing manifests and successful retention tag enforcement; 6) Integration tests and a smoke test checklist in the PR.
notes: We intentionally keep the envelope lightweight to avoid storing PII; normalizer will redact any detected PII using existing redact service before canonicalization. Use new evidence schema to make downstream audit export and snapshotting deterministic. Prefer append-only manifests and gzipped .jsonl bundles to reduce object count.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype ingestor + normalizer (2 sprints) -> Phase 2: KMS signer & manifest builder (1 sprint) -> Phase 3: Backfill adapter + integration tests + staging run with two pilot customers. Rollout via feature flag per-customer and region.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental ingestion of PII or large binary blobs; Mitigation: enforce size limits, use redact-service, reject >10MB inline payloads and surface presigned upload flow. Risk: key compromise; Mitigation: sign only metadata and store keys in customer KMS alias where required, rotate keys every quarter. Risk: long manifest generation time for large bundles; Mitigation: stream checksums and generate incremental manifests.
